source.title: Pitfalls in Evaluating Interpretability Agents
source.authors: Tal Haklay; Nikhil Prakash; Sana Pandey; Antonio Torralba; Aaron Mueller; Jacob Andreas; T. Shaham; Yonatan Belinkov

page_placements.theme: Weight geometry partly reflects functional classes and pathways

record.tranche_reason: The study uses component weight swaps and a behavior-based similarity metric to assess whether IOI heads grouped in the expert-defined clusters behave similarly. This conceptually tests cluster coherence, but it does not reproduce the original faithfulness, completeness, or minimality tests.
record.gate_note: The IOI circuit is supplied as an already identified circuit. The study's pairwise swap experiments and cluster-coherence measurements bear on whether its expert-defined IOI head groups share functional behavior. The reported circuit size and cluster count are task setup details, not new tests of the original circuit. The IOI noise-sensitivity results concern the interpretability agents' explanation accuracy, not GPT-2's IOI behavior, and are not rows for these claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study takes the IOI circuit as given ground truth for evaluating interpretability agents, using an 18-head, 6-cluster subset rather than the original 26 heads in 7 classes. The swap-based silhouette of the expert IOI clusters (0.21 vs random -0.28) and the head (10,0) distance plot are presented to validate the authors' own intrinsic metric ('As expected... Expert clusters achieve much higher scores'). They are not offered as a test of the circuit. No faithfulness, completeness, minimality, backup, cross-model, method or prompt-variant result on the IOI circuit itself is reported.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that replication-based evaluation of interpretability agents can mislead because expert explanations can be subjective or incomplete, outcome comparisons ignore the research process, and LLMs may memorize or guess published findings. Claude Opus 4.1 recalled the IOI circuit from memory. They propose a swap-based intrinsic metric as a limited proof of concept. They draw no conclusion about the IOI circuit's validity.
record.recipe_differences: The original claim uses faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria for a circuit. This study evaluates cluster coherence through pairwise KQ/OV swaps, Jensen–Shannon distances, and silhouette scores; it does not apply the original circuit tests.

fits_no_version.finding: Under KQ/OV weight-swap Jensen–Shannon distances on 40 IOI examples, the expert GPT-2-small IOI head clusters score silhouette 0.21 vs random -0.28 ± 0.07. Other name-mover heads lie closer to (10,0) than heads from other clusters.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Heads in the same IOI functional class are approximately interchangeable by weight swap, i.e. the class partition is functionally coherent.

fits_no_version.finding: Expert Pythia-160M IOI clusters (Tigges et al.) score silhouette 0.10 vs random -0.24 ± 0.08. Pythia head 2.6, labelled a previous-token head, attends most to the previous token in only 42% of 150 PILE examples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: IOI-like head classes in Pythia-160M are weakly coherent, and some component labels there are ambiguous.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 9th BlackboxNLP Workshop: Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP
record.problems: The IOI swap-based analysis uses 40 task examples and evaluates cluster coherence rather than directly testing IOI performance under circuit ablation. The study does not test the original faithfulness, completeness, or minimality criteria.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted agentic and one-shot cluster-quality scores in Table 2 because they evaluate the systems' generated clusterings, not the original IOI circuit's claimed classes. Omitted IOI noise-sensitivity results in Figures 6 and 8 because they measure agent explanation accuracy. Omitted entity-tracking analyses because they concern a different task.

untested.parts: Circuit size and classes, faithfulness, completeness, minimality and the head roles under the original patching criteria.
Same head classes in other models, sizes or checkpoints, and reuse for other tasks. The Pythia-160M IOI clusters from Tigges et al. are only used as agent ground truth.
Recovery of the circuit by other discovery methods, ablations or metrics.
Dependence of faithfulness or completeness on ablation, metric or prompt distribution.
Mechanism across name orders, templates or more names.

missing.what: Expert-cluster silhouette for IOI in Pythia-160M (0.10 vs random -0.24 ± 0.08). Relevant only to the fits_no_version coherence finding.
Pythia head 2.6 previous-token attention in only 42% of 150 PILE examples.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' with a V1 supports label overreaches. The expert-cluster silhouette is circular metric validation on a reduced 18-head clustering, not a test of the IOI circuit claims. The noise-sensitivity and memorization results concern the agents, not GPT-2.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests expert-cluster coherence through swap-based output similarity, but not the claimed circuit size or seven classes, faithfulness, completeness, minimality, or the stated roles through the original patching criteria.
Backup-head takeover after ablating main name-mover heads.
Whether the same mechanism holds across other models, sizes, checkpoints, or tasks.
Whether other circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or metrics recover essentially the same circuit.
Whether the IOI circuit's faithfulness or completeness changes with ablation, metric, or prompt distribution, or whether it explains only part of IOI behavior.
Whether the same mechanism holds across name orders, templates, or prompts with more names.

rows.subject: GPT-2-Small
rows.operation_detail: Silhouette score for the expert-defined IOI head clustering, calculated from pairwise swap-based distances.
rows.note: The expert-defined clustering scores higher than the random-clustering baseline. This bears on functional coherence of the reported head groups, not on the circuit's overall faithfulness, completeness, or minimality.
rows.check: This is a swap-based cluster-coherence score used to validate the authors' metric against expert clusters. It measures neither V1's circuit criteria nor its head roles. The clustering is an 18-head, 6-class subset that omits backup name movers and some heads, so it is not the original 26-head, 7-class circuit.

relation.reason: The IOI circuit supplies components and reference explanations for evaluating interpretability systems. Agreement under the swap metric does not independently establish the claimed circuit.

tranche.reason: The reported cluster-coherence results evaluate the authors' interpretation metric using published IOI groups as reference clusters; they do not assess the claim versions' circuit criteria or mechanism.

source_check.notes: The GPT-2-Small reference contains 18 heads in six clusters. Section 4.1 separately questions Pythia-160M head (2,6)'s previous-token label: previous-token attention is maximal on 42% of 150 PILE examples; this does not establish a different IOI mechanism.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The expert clustering scores above the random-clustering baseline, and the reported name-mover head is closer by swap-based distance to heads in its own cluster than to heads in other clusters (R1, R3). This supports cluster coherence only, not the full claim's criteria.
